name: dataset/models.py
summary: Defines the core Dataset and DatasetTable Django ORM models that persist dataset metadata and tabular structure to the relational database.
purpose: Provides the canonical data schema and domain objects for the dataset management subsystem, enabling storage, retrieval, and relational integrity between datasets and their constituent tables.
responsibilities: Define database schema for dataset and table metadata
Enforce referential integrity between Dataset and DatasetTable via ForeignKey relationships
Expose a domain-specific ORM interface for the dataset service and API layer
Map application configuration (e.g., user model from settings) into model relationships
inputs: ORM queries from the dataset service and views
Parent Dataset identifiers when creating DatasetTable records
outputs: QuerySet objects for downstream serializers and services
architecture_notes: Acts as the data access and domain layer within a layered Django architecture. The presence of an explicit service layer (dataset_service.py) and DRF serializers indicates a design leaning toward separation of persistence from business orchestration. The ForeignKey relationship suggests Dataset is an aggregate root with DatasetTable as a child entity. Importing settings implies use of swappable user relationships or dynamic configuration, which is standard but couples the model to project configuration.
improvements: Add database indexes on frequently queried ForeignKey fields and status flags to prevent N+1 issues and slow lookups at scale
Introduce a custom ModelManager or QuerySet to encapsulate common query patterns (e.g., prefetch_related for tables) and reduce duplication in the service layer
Add type hints and verbose_name/meta options to improve maintainability and admin readability
Consider splitting DatasetTable into a separate module if the domain grows, or introducing an abstract TimestampedModel base if both classes share audit fields
Evaluate adding validation constraints (e.g., unique_together, CheckConstraint) at the database level to enforce domain invariants closer to storage
